title: Chapter 27
content:
A live video feed flickered on Jakyeong’s smartphone screen, showing Kang Il-hyun knocking firmly on his bedroom door. Watching the man linger in the hallway, Jakyeong typed out a swift reply.

On screen, Il-hyun read the message, his dark eyes fixing onto the locked wooden door with an unreadable gaze. Biting his lower lip, Jakyeong tapped out the follow-up text:

[I took my medicine. I think I just need to sleep it off. Thank you for your consideration.]

Please don't kick the damn door off its hinges. Knowing Il-hyun's unhinged temper, tearing the room apart wouldn't have been out of character.

To Jakyeong's immense relief, Il-hyun turned on his heel and walked away. Closing his eyes, Jakyeong let out a long, silent breath. Installing concealed micro-cameras in the guest suite's lounge and bedroom just in case had proven to be a stroke of pure tactical genius.

Stowing the phone in his sling bag, Jakyeong dropped low, surveying the perimeter of the Doksan-dong compound. The corrugated iron gates were chained shut, with not a soul visible on guard. Yet given the fleet of vehicles parked in the gravel lot, the place was far from empty.

Moving like a wraith, he slipped beneath each parked vehicle, mounting magnetic brick charges to their fuel tanks and syncing their digital timers to his tactical wristwatch.

The hum of an approaching engine cut through the quiet. Tucking himself into the blind spot of a parked cargo van, he watched a sleek black sedan roll into the lot. The engine died, and a lone enforcer stepped out into the night air.

Jakyeong closed the distance without a whisper of sound, reaching out to twist the man's neck with brutal efficiency.

Crack.

The thug collapsed without even managing a gasp. Snatching the key fob from the dead man's fingers, Jakyeong slid into the driver's seat.

He strapped in, fired up the engine, and slammed his foot flat against the floorboards.

ROAR—!

The sedan rocketed across the gravel lot, plowing full-throttle straight into the warehouse’s corrugated steel doors.

BOOM!

The heavy doors buckled and tore off their tracks with a deafening screech of rending metal. The impact whipped Jakyeong against his harness before snapping him back into the headrest. Wincing against the shockwave, he looked through the cracked windshield—the hood was crumpled like a sheet of tinfoil.

Inside the warehouse, roughly a dozen men stood frozen, staring in sheer, dumbfounded shock. Plates of food and bottles of soju covered the folding tables before them—he’d crashed their late dinner.

The moment Jakyeong kicked the driver's door open and stepped out into the dust, the men realized he wasn't one of their own. As one, a dozen hands reached inside leather jackets, drawing gleaming sashimi blades.

Jakyeong let out a cold, venomous chuckle behind his tactical mask.

"Knock knock. Forgot to use the doorbell... hope I'm not interrupting dinner?"

A thug with tight perm-curled hair stepped forward, his scarred face twisting into a feral sneer. "Who the fuck are you, punk? What crew are you with?"

Crew? I'm an orphan with no family, you piece of shit.

Jakyeong drew his suppressed pistol, leveled the muzzle dead-center between the man's eyes, and squeezed the trigger.

Phfft.

The back of the leader's skull burst open in a red mist. Three men flanking him lunged forward with blades raised. Moving with terrifying, fluid speed, Jakyeong drilled three consecutive rounds into the exact same fatal coordinate.

Phfft. Phfft. Phfft.

Three bodies hit the concrete floor in a heap.

The remaining enforcers froze in place, paralyzed by the sheer, mechanical precision of the slaughter. Seeing their comrades' skulls detonated in the blink of an eye, the blade-wielding thugs hesitated, trading frantic, terrified glances.

"Anyone else?" Jakyeong asked mildly.

"..."

"No takers? Good. Mind if I wrap up my business and get going?"

A sudden shift of air at his back warned him just in time. A steel blade whistled toward his ribs.

Jakyeong pivoted on his heel, letting the cold edge graze his jacket, caught the attacker by his hair, and wrenched his neck backward until the spine cracked. At the same instant, the remaining crew broke their paralysis, roaring as they swarmed him in a desperate, frantic charge.

Drawing a combat trench knife from his hip, Jakyeong drove the serrated blade repeatedly into the pinned thug's throat—stab, rip, twist—unleashing an arterial fountain. Hurlng the gurgling body into the charging pack, he put a fresh round through the dying man's skull and opened rapid-fire on the rest.

Phfft-phfft-phfft!

The smarter ones dropped their blades and bolted for the rear exits, but Jakyeong tracked their silhouettes with mechanical ruthlessness, dropping every runner with a round through the brain stem.

In under thirty seconds, thirteen grown men were reduced to a pile of leaking corpses on the concrete floor.

Jakyeong paced through the carnage, checking the bodies and putting a final insurance round through anyone still twitching. Leaving trash like this alive only bred more filth. Ejecting his spent magazine, he slapped in a fresh clip with a crisp click and moved deeper into the facility.

Past the main floor, he found a heavy steel door secured with a heavy iron padlock. He drew his pistol and blasted the cylinder to pieces.

Kicking the door open, he found no children—only mountains of cardboard boxes stacked shoulder-high. He sliced open one of the crates, revealing hundreds of innocent-looking bags of commercial sugar.

He drove his blade through the center of a sugar bag, digging inside until his fingers caught a thumb-sized ziplock packet filled with crystalline white powder. He dabbed a grain onto the tip of his tongue.

Methamphetamine. High-purity ice.

Spitting onto the floor with a disgusted Ptooey!, he scanned the warehouse. There were easily hundreds of crates.

Finding the kids took priority over burning the product. Leaving the narcotics behind, he pressed deeper into the complex. The facility was deathly quiet, but he kept his sidearm raised in high-ready.

Near the back wall, he spotted a narrow, weathered wooden hatch—barely wide enough for a single man to squeeze through.

He pulled the hatch open, revealing a steep concrete flight leading into a subterranean cellar. Switching on his tactical pen-light, he descended step by measured step. Thud. Thud.

A nauseating stench of stagnant waste and rotting biological matter billowed up from the depths. As his boots touched the bottom landing, two bloated sewer rats scrambled into the dark.

Sweeping the pen-light across the cellar, he spotted a reinforced door bolted from the outside with an iron bar.

Jakyeong leveled his sidearm, blew the lock apart, and the warped door swung inward. He stepped behind the frame, raised his weapon alongside the light, and snapped into a tactical low-ready sweep.

Through the narrow opening, a small silhouette came into view.

Jakyeong lowered his muzzle instantly, keeping only the pen-light illuminated.

Crouched in the corner was a young girl, clutching a jagged stone in her fist, trembling violently from head to toe. Jakyeong recognized her immediately: the teenage drop-runner from the alley. Her face was heavily bruised and swollen from a brutal beating, and huddled behind her were five younger children, holding their breath in terrified silence.

Seeing her knuckles turning white around that pitiful stone, Jakyeong reached up and slowly pulled his tactical mask down beneath his chin.

The girl’s eyes widened in stunned recognition.

"You're not... actually going to throw that rock at me, are you?" Jakyeong murmured softly.

Her bruised face crumpled, tears welling up in her hollow, exhausted eyes. Jakyeong stood there awkwardly, utterly unsure of what to say.

The girl let the stone clatter to the floor and wiped her eyes with the dirty sleeve of her jacket. Jakyeong stepped forward, checking on the rest of the children. But as he counted them, his stomach dropped.

There were only six. There had been seven in the van.

"Where's the last one?"

Another boy pushed himself upright from the corner. Realizing the man wasn't there to butcher them, the children slowly lowered their defenses.

"He's... he's dead..." the boy whispered, his voice cracking.

Jakyeong felt an icy clamp tighten around his chest. "How?"

"They beat him... until he stopped moving..."

A sharp, searing ache ripped through Jakyeong's gut. Because I dropped them at the precinct.

He shoved the guilt down into a cold, dark box—there was time to drown in self-loathing later. Getting these kids out before reinforcements swarmed the area was the only mission that mattered. Spotting a young child who couldn't stand on bruised legs, Jakyeong hoisted the boy onto his back, instructing the older kids to link hands and stay tight.

Climbing back into the warehouse, the glaring work lights washed over them. Seeing the floor carpeted with bodies and blown-out skulls, the children didn't scream or scatter. In that chamber of horrors, the older ones simply reached out, silently covering the eyes of the little ones.

Jakyeong led them outside, smashed the side window of an undamaged utility van in the lot, unlocked the door, and ushered the kids inside.

"Stay inside. Do not move an inch until I come back."

Giving them a firm, steady look, Jakyeong grabbed his sling bag and strode back into the narcotics bay.

He found a drum of industrial kerosene, dragged it over, and doused the entire mountain of sugar-cut methamphetamine boxes. Flicking his Zippo open, he tossed the flame onto the puddle.

FWOOSH!

Flames roared to life, greedily swallowing the multi-million-dollar stash.

Moving quickly, he located the heavy LPG propane tanks the crew had used for their outdoor cooking burners. He cranked the master valves wide open and kicked the cylinders over—HIIISSSSSS. Pressurized gas flooded the air with an acrid, chemical stink. Behind him, the fire was already racing up the support beams, licking at the ceiling trusses.

Jakyeong stepped outside, slammed the warehouse doors shut, and sprinted back to the van.

He pulled wire cutters and a flathead from his kit, ripped the ignition shroud apart, and stripped the leads. He crossed the hot-wires, but the starter only clicked—Ch-ch-ch.

Damn it. It's been too long since I hot-wired an old rig.

Checking his wristwatch, barely ten minutes remained before the timed charges on the parking lot vehicles detonated.

Taking a slow, controlled breath, he matched the correct ignition leads and sparked them together.

VROOM!

The heavy van shuddered to life. Jakyeong let out a breathless, triumphant laugh. Shifting into gear, he stomped the throttle, peeling out of the compound before the chain-reaction explosions could tear the lot apart.

One, two, three, four, five, six...

Wang Ryun’s face was an absolute picture of existential distress.

Jakyeong had taken off on a high-end Kawasaki with an arsenal of black-market military hardware, only to return with the bike mysteriously gone and half a dozen filthy, street-urchin refugees in tow.

The kids were currently huddled around the office table, frantically inhaling bowls of jajangmyeon and sweet-and-sour pork like starving wolves.

"Did you... give birth to these?" Ryun asked, dumbfounded.

"Not in the mood for jokes, Ryun."

Ryun waved his hands frantically. "Look, rescuing them is great and all, but dumping them on me?! What do I look like, a daycare center?!"

"I can't take them with me."

"Then hand them over to the cops!"

"I'll give you a broker's cut."

"You think this is about money?!"

"Five percent of my contract fee."

"..."

"Take it or leave it."

"Hang on a second," Ryun cleared his throat, suddenly looking deeply thoughtful. "I'm just calculating the logistics of the best placement facility."

Jakyeong smiled faintly.

After running through his contacts, Ryun settled on a Catholic parish he attended regularly. The resident priest ran an unlisted shelter for runaway and orphaned youth, making it the safest haven in the country.

To an outsider, the idea of an arms dealer attending mass was absurd, but Ryun had been a devout Catholic since childhood, carrying the baptismal name Antonio. He’d even refused to take wet-work jobs on Sundays back in his active mercenary days. Wang Han had always mocked Ryun for lacking professional discipline, but Jakyeong secretly envied the man. Having faith was a luxury Jakyeong had never experienced—he’d never believed in a higher power, nor had he ever had a reason to pray.

After polishing off his bowl of black-bean noodles, Jakyeong switched on the wall-mounted television.

A breaking news alert flashed across the screen: a massive industrial explosion had leveled a warehouse in Doksan-dong, with fire crews battling the four-alarm blaze. The children’s dark, marble-like eyes locked onto the screen in stunned silence.

Jakyeong clicked the TV off, stepped out into the rear lot, and lit a cigarette.

He drew the smoke deep into his lungs, his cheeks hollowing, before exhaling a thick plume into the cool night air. The sky above was pristine, completely cloudless.

As he gazed up at the pale moon, the shop door creaked open behind him. Expecting Ryun, he turned—only to find the teenage girl standing nervously under the awning.

"Thank... thank you..." she stammered in a tiny, fragile voice.

Before Jakyeong could reply, she turned and bolted back inside like a startled deer.

A heavy, suffocating warmth pooled in Jakyeong’s chest. When he’d first crossed paths with her in that filthy alley, he’d thought she was the spitting image of his own cursed childhood.

He had been wrong. She was infinitely better than he had ever been.

The image of that terrified girl—standing bruised and shivering in the dark, clutching a jagged stone just to protect the younger children behind her—was a sight he knew he would carry with him for the rest of his life.

Snubbing his cigarette out against the brick wall, Jakyeong tilted his head back toward the night sky.

Rescuing the kids was done. Now... the real nightmare was figuring out how to sneak back into Kang Il-hyun’s fortress without getting caught.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Philopon / Hiropon (필로폰): The historical East Asian street slang for methamphetamine (derived from the trade name Philopon used in Japan during WWII). In Korean underworld terminology, it is commonly referred to as "ice" or "the white powder."

  • Jajangmyeon & Tangsuyuk (짜장면 / 탕수육): Black bean noodles and crispy sweet-and-sour pork are South Korea's ultimate comfort takeout food—traditionally served to celebrate moving into a new home, hard labor, or given to hungry children as a hearty, satisfying meal.

  • Catholic Names in Korean Underworld (세례명 안토니오): South Korea has a significant Roman Catholic population, and it is culturally common for believers to adopt Christian baptismal names (se-rye-myeong). An arms dealer meticulously observing Sunday Sabbath and holding a baptismal name adds a layer of ironic, grounded texture to Ryun's character.
